candidates.title: [Bug]: compiler stack overflow when a parameter default calls its own function
candidates.body:
### Description
The compiler crashes with a Go `fatal error: stack overflow` when a defaultable parameter's default expression recursively calls the function that declares it. The recursion is in type resolution of the function signature (`resolveFunctionSignature` → `ensureResolved` → `resolveFunctionCallArgs` → `resolveFunctionSignature` in `semantics/internal/types/type_resolver.go`).

Spec §5.6.2: "Whether a parameter is defaultable, and what its default is, do not affect the shape of the function", so the signature can be resolved without the default. The default "is turned into a closure that computes the default value for the parameter using the values of previous parameters"; here it refers only to the previous parameter `n`, so the program is valid. A compiler crash is a bug in any case.

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

function rec(int n, int d = n > 0 ? rec(n - 1) : 0) returns int {
    return n + d;
}

public function main() {
    io:println(rec(3)); // @output 6
}
```

**Actual:**
```
runtime: goroutine stack exceeds 1000000000-byte limit
fatal error: stack overflow
```
**Expected:** prints `6`.

### Affected Version(s)
nutcracker `main` @ d69c341a58ce66f78559965ddfe27877a34f31d0

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, Go 1.27.1, `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`

### Related area
Type checker

### Related issue(s) (optional)
Not a duplicate of #1618 (index out of range on function type with unnamed param) or #1483 (module var init cycle through a parameter default).

candidates.title: [Bug]: `isolated function` type without a signature ignores the `isolated` qualifier
[Bug]: invalid UTF-8 and disallowed code points in source string literals are accepted
candidates.body:
### Description
Source bytes inside a string literal are not validated as UTF-8, and disallowed code points are not rejected. An encoded surrogate (bytes `ED A0 80` = U+D800) or a stray `0xFF` byte inside `"..."` compiles; each stray byte becomes its own "character", producing a `string` value that is not a sequence of Unicode scalar values (`string:fromBytes(s.toBytes())` then returns an error). Raw C0 controls (NUL, VT, 0x1F), C1 controls (U+0085) and non-characters (U+FFFF, U+FDD0, U+10FFFE) inside literals are also accepted silently.

Spec §4 (Lexical structure): the source octets are "interpreted as the UTF-8 encoding of a sequence of code points and must comply with the requirements of RFC 3629" and "The sequence of code points must not contain any of the following disallowed code points: surrogates (0xD800 to 0xDFFF), non-characters, C0 control characters other than white space ..., C1 control characters (0x80 to 0x9F)". Also "the grammar notation ^X does not allow the above disallowed code points", so `StringChar` cannot match them. §5.3.1: strings contain only Unicode scalar values excluding surrogates. Escaped forms (`"\u{D800}"`) are already rejected correctly.

### Steps to Reproduce
The file contains raw bytes, so create it with `printf`:
```sh
printf 'import ballerina/io;\n\npublic function main() {\n    string s = "a\xed\xa0\x80b"; // @error\n    io:println(s.length());\n    io:println(string:fromBytes(s.toBytes()) is error);\n    io:println(s[1] == s[1]);\n    foreach var c in s { io:println(c.toBytes()); }\n}\n' > invalid-utf8-source-e.bal
```
Content (with the invalid bytes shown as `<ED A0 80>`):
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    string s = "a<ED A0 80>b"; // @error
    io:println(s.length());
    io:println(string:fromBytes(s.toBytes()) is error);
    io:println(s[1] == s[1]);
    foreach var c in s { io:println(c.toBytes()); }
}
```
**Actual:** compiles and prints `5`, `true`, `true`, `[97]`, `[237]`, `[160]`, `[128]`, `[98]`.
**Expected:** a compile error (invalid UTF-8 / disallowed code point in source). Same for `\xff`, `\x00`, `\x0b`, U+0085, U+FFFF, U+FDD0 written raw inside a literal.

### Affected Version(s)
nutcracker `main` @ d69c341a58ce66f78559965ddfe27877a34f31d0

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, Go 1.27.1, `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`

### Related area
Parser

### Related issue(s) (optional)
Related: #1456 (BOM / newline normalization), #1348 (invalid `\u{...}` escapes, fixed), #1619 (non-ASCII treated as hex digits).
